newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares ease after record highs.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares ease after record highs.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Wednesday with players becoming cautious after Tuesday's record gains and likely to remain so on Thursday, dealers said.
"The market has climbed nicely in the past few days so it is not so strange that people want to collect themselves somewhat," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index fell 0.47 point to 121.80 in low overall bourse turnover of 691 million crowns. The KFX September future fell 0.45 point to 121.75 with 724 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Despite steady interest in bank paper of late, Unidanmark stumbled four crowns down to 272 crowns and Den Danske Bank slipped a crown to 429 crowns, hobbled by a bond market treading water amid U.S. rate rise worries.
Tele Danmark eased three crowns to 277 and Novo Nordisk shed four crowns to 897 crowns.
SAS, however, continued to climb, closing up one crown at 67.
Although down from Tuesday the KFX was well up on last Wednesday's 119.86 and the closing 119.61 of a month ago -- a record high at the time.
